"source_index": 0, "source_unit": "This study explores the role of carbon labelling in the food sector as a tool to reduce carbon emissions and promote sustainable consumption, focusing specifically on sandwich products including the ham and cheese sandwich. Carbon labelling informs consumers about the carbon emissions associated with a product\u2019s production, distribution, and disposal. Using mixed qualitative and quantitative methodologies, the study investigates consumer perceptions of carbon labelling and its impact on purchasing behavior, while also analyzing carbon emissions within the food industry. A Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) was conducted to evaluate the carbon footprints of two sandwich recipes: a ham and cheese sandwich and a cheese and mayonnaise sandwich. The LCA results showed that the ham and cheese sandwich has a significantly higher carbon footprint, ranging between 1053 and 1070 g CO2 equivalent, compared to 700 to 750 g CO2 equivalent for the cheese and mayonnaise sandwich. Key contributors to these emissions include ingredient production, packaging, and energy use during manufacturing. Collaboration with a sandwich maker allowed comprehensive data collection and a detailed carbon footprint analysis spanning the entire production process. Survey results highlight a disparity between consumer awareness and behavior: while 68.6% of respondents recognize the importance of carbon labelling, only 26.9% report that this influences their purchasing choices. This gap suggests that although consumers express concern about carbon footprints, carbon labelling alone may not strongly drive behavior change. The study emphasizes that educating consumers, standardizing carbon labelling practices, and modifying sandwich recipes\u2014such as potentially reformulating the ham and cheese sandwich\u2014could enhance the effectiveness of carbon labelling. complication occurring 8 years after inguinal hernia repair using a polypropylene plug mesh. Mesh infection is a known short-term complication following hernia repair, but it seldom leads to the development of an ileocutaneous fistula. The patient, a 67-year-old male, initially underwent right inguinal hernia repair with a polypropylene plug. Years later, he presented with skin ulceration and pus in the right groin, and was eventually diagnosed with an enterocutaneous fistula. Laparoscopic exploration revealed that the ileum near the fistula was closely adherent to the abdominal wall. During surgery, after careful separation of the bowel loop, a 2 \u00d7 3 cm defect was identified on the ileal surface. Further laparotomy showed that the polypropylene plug mesh was embedded inside the ileum. The plug was completely removed, and an ileum side-to-side anastomosis was performed to restore bowel integrity. The patient recovered well, being discharged two weeks post-operation, and six-month follow-up showed complete wound healing without hernia recurrence. This case highlights the importance of considering late-onset ileocutaneous fistula as a differential diagnosis in patients presenting with inflammation or abscess at the site of prior hernia repair with polypropylene plug mesh. The report emphasizes that laparoscopic exploration should be prioritized for suspected intestinal fistulas following such repairs. Laparoscopic exploration revealed that the ileum near the fistula was closely adherent to the abdominal wall. During surgery, after careful separation of the bowel loop, a 2 \u00d7 3 cm defect was identified on the ileal surface. Further laparotomy showed that the polypropylene plug mesh was embedded inside the ileum. The plug was completely removed, and an ileum side-to-side anastomosis was performed to restore bowel integrity. The patient recovered well, being discharged two weeks post-operation, and six-month follow-up showed complete wound healing without hernia recurrence. This case highlights the importance of considering late-onset ileocutaneous fistula as a differential diagnosis in patients presenting with inflammation or abscess at the site of prior hernia repair with polypropylene plug mesh. The report emphasizes that laparoscopic exploration should be prioritized for suspected intestinal fistulas following such repairs. Additionally, it underlines the necessity of customizing the approach to mesh removal based on laparoscopic findings, particularly when dealing with complications involving polypropylene plug mesh integration into adjacent bowel tissue. Findings show that only a small minority of consumers expressed willingness to buy wine (canned). The majority rejected this option, citing concerns about low quality perception and a lack of positive regard for non-traditional wine packaging. A key obstacle to the wider acceptance of wine (canned) is the lack of consumer knowledge about this packaging format. Nonetheless, the study highlights potential opportunities for canned wine to appeal to diverse groups of wine drinkers and suit various consumption occasions. This suggests that canned wine could expand market options for winemakers, particularly by attracting non-regular consumers who may appreciate the convenience and novelty of canned wine. Results reveal that the understory of eucalyptus plantations is characterized by a significant abundance of native species. These native plants are mostly in early succession stages, occupying the understory of eucalyptus plants and contributing minimally to the basal area. Interestingly, the basal areas of native species in eucalyptus plantation sites adjacent to natural forests are comparable to those in young slash-and-burn fallows (0\u20135 years old), which also occur near natural forests. Moreover, eucalyptus plantations established in savannahs far from natural forests can function as catalysts for the natural regeneration of native species, promoting recovery processes that would not occur without them. In contrast, eucalyptus plants located on the edge of or within natural forests tend to slow down native species regeneration, which would otherwise progress more rapidly without the influence of EP. Overall, this study underscores the critical role of the spatial landscape context in determining how eucalyptus plantations affect the conservation and restoration of tropical forest ecosystems. Specifically, the research investigates the relationships and drivers of ecosystem services\u2014namely forage provisioning and water retention\u2014in degraded alpine shrub meadows, a key component of the grassland ecosystem on the northeastern QTP. The study analyzes how these two critical ecosystem services change across different levels of degradation within the grassland ecosystem. Findings reveal that degradation causes forage supply in the alpine shrub meadow to increase by 23.6%, while water retention decreases by 27.07%. Trade-offs between these services vary with degradation intensity: light and moderate degradation favors water retention services, whereas heavy and extreme degradation favors forage provisioning. Overall, the findings emphasize the complex dynamics within grassland ecosystems, where balancing multiple ecosystem services under degradation pressures is challenging. "This study evaluated the agreement among veterinarians in detecting abnormal lung sounds in veal lung (raw) auscultations to improve the diagnosis of calf bronchopneumonia. Forty lung sounds collected from veal lung (raw) samples across four veal calf farms, which housed between 495 and 815 animals, were assessed online by 10 veterinarians. After a short tutorial aimed at standardizing lung sound definitions, the raters identified the presence of abnormal sounds and categorized them into wheezes, crackles, or bronchial sounds. Various agreement indicators were used to measure consistency among raters, including raw percentage of agreement (PA), Gwet's agreement coefficient type 1 (AC1), Krippendorff's alpha (Ka), and Fleiss kappa (KFleiss), with benchmarks applied in the absence of a gold standard. The results indicated fair to good agreement levels across almost all lung sound indicators in veal lung (raw) assessments. Specifically, for detecting any abnormal lung sound in veal lung (raw), the PA was 0.781, AC1 was 0.646, Ka was 0.403, and KFleiss was 0.293. Agreement for wheezes showed PA at 0.769, AC1 at 0.615, Ka at 0.426, and KFleiss at 0.425. Crackle detection agreement values were PA 0.754, AC1 0.643, Ka 0.21, and KFleiss 0.208. For bronchial sounds, agreements were lower: PA 0.636, AC1 0.345, Ka 0.182, and KFleiss 0.18. The study concludes that the level of agreement among veterinarians auscultating veal lung (raw) respiratory sounds is better than previously reported. Nonetheless, further improvements are needed to enhance reliability and consistency in veal lung (raw) lung auscultation, which is crucial for the effective and routine diagnosis of calf bronchopneumonia on veal calf farms.", "weight": 0.0955217933633972}, {"claim_id": "SRC-0002", "text": "Forty lung sounds collected from veal lung (raw) samples across four veal calf farms, which housed between 495 and 815 animals, were assessed online by 10 veterinarians.", "source_index": 0, "source_unit": "This study evaluated the agreement among veterinarians in detecting abnormal lung sounds in veal lung (raw) auscultations to improve the diagnosis of calf bronchopneumonia. Forty lung sounds collected from veal lung (raw) samples across four veal calf farms, which housed between 495 and 815 animals, were assessed online by 10 veterinarians. After a short tutorial aimed at standardizing lung sound definitions, the raters identified the presence of abnormal sounds and categorized them into wheezes, crackles, or bronchial sounds. Various agreement indicators were used to measure consistency among raters, including raw percentage of agreement (PA), Gwet's agreement coefficient type 1 (AC1), Krippendorff's alpha (Ka), and Fleiss kappa (KFleiss), with benchmarks applied in the absence of a gold standard. The results indicated fair to good agreement levels across almost all lung sound indicators in veal lung (raw) assessments. Specifically, for detecting any abnormal lung sound in veal lung (raw), the PA was 0.781, AC1 was 0.646, Ka was 0.403, and KFleiss was 0.293. Agreement for wheezes showed PA at 0.769, AC1 at 0.615, Ka at 0.426, and KFleiss at 0.425. Crackle detection agreement values were PA 0.754, AC1 0.643, Ka 0.21, and KFleiss 0.208. NSSH was harvested during its main season from September to February, and chemical analyses were performed to determine fatty acids, protein, and vitamins A and D in the belly flaps. These values indicate that the belly flap from NSSH contains approximately twice the amount of vitamin D, EPA, and DHA compared to NSSH fillet (raw). During alcoholic fermentation, compounds such as esters and some alcohols increased significantly, whereas alcohols, terpenoids, and certain esters decreased notably throughout the fermentation processes. Advanced analytical techniques, including E-nose and E-tongue analyses combined with principal component analysis (PCA) and discriminant factor analysis (DFA), effectively distinguished the samples at various fermentation stages, reflecting changes in the lemon peel-derived product\u2019s chemical profile. The research aimed to evaluate the effects of three different processing methods on the quality of elderberry wine. These methods included: no extended maceration followed by hot water treatment (EC0); 2 days of cold soak maceration with hot water treatment (EC2); and boiling elderberry fruits (EB) prior to alcoholic fermentation. Findings revealed that while ethanol, glycerol, total acidity, volatile acidity, and tannin levels in elderberry wines were not significantly affected by the treatments, the wine pH was influenced. Notably, the cold soak maceration method in EC2 did not enhance antioxidant extraction in elderberry wine. Results indicated that the wheat food product containing tuna by-products had a higher fatty acid content compared to the one with sea bass. Texture profile analysis revealed that both fish-containing wheat food products exhibited lower hardness and fracturability than the reference wheat pasta. However, cohesiveness was higher in the tuna wheat food product, while the sea bass variant showed brighter color attributes. The addition of fish by-products affected other technological aspects of the wheat food products, causing decreases in weight gain and swelling index but increases in cooking losses during preparation. Sensory analysis identified clear distinctions related to homogeneity, typical aroma, fish flavor, fish odor, and elasticity among the wheat food products studied. Importantly, the study suggests reducing tuna content to less than 3% in the wheat food product to enhance its sensory qualities without compromising nutritional benefits. Overall, the research concludes that integrating fish by-products into wheat food products like pasta can improve their nutritional profile, particularly by enriching them with valuable fatty acids. However, balancing sensory acceptability remains crucial, especially for formulations involving tuna by-products. Cystic Echinococcosis (CE) is a parasitic disease affecting cattle, sheep, and humans, with fertile cysts containing viable protoscoleces. The research explores how host species and cyst location influence protoscolex gene expression, focusing on samples from sheep lung (raw) and liver cysts, alongside cattle liver cyst data obtained from the NCBI SRA database. Transcriptomic data were collected from six sheep lung CE cysts (raw) and six liver CE cysts, showing no significant differences in gene expression between protoscoleces from the liver and lung within or across individual sheep. Principal component and differential expression analyses confirmed that cyst location in sheep (lung versus liver) does not substantially affect protoscolex transcriptomes. In contrast, significant differences emerged when comparing protoscoleces from sheep lung (raw) and liver cysts to those from cattle liver cysts. Differential expression analysis revealed immune-related gene variation linked to host species rather than cyst location. In cattle, seven genes were significantly upregulated in protoscoleces from liver cysts, while in sheep, three genes, including antigen B, tegument antigen, and arginase-2, were upregulated in metacestodes derived from lung (raw) and liver CE cysts. Basigin was notably upregulated in cattle samples. These findings suggest that the host species\u2014sheep versus cattle\u2014is a critical determinant of immune-related gene expression in Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto protoscoleces. Importantly, the data from sheep lung (raw) cysts highlight that parasite gene expression is consistent across lung and liver cysts within sheep but differs significantly from cattle hosts. Here is a concise summary of the text within 350 words, based on the available information: --- This study evaluated the effects of incorporating raw chickpea seeds (RCKP, cv. Burnas) as an alternative protein source to soybean meal (SBM) in diets for young turkeys (1 to 70 days old). Using a 4 \u00d7 2 factorial design, four RCKP inclusion levels (0, 80, 120, and 240 g/kg, replacing SBM) and two enzyme supplementation levels (0 or 0.2 g/kg phytase) were assessed for their impact on growth performance, carcass traits, bone mineralization, and plasma profiles. The results revealed that turkey body weight gain increased significantly with higher RCKP levels, while feed intake and feed conversion ratio (FCR) remained unaffected. Carcass yield, breast and leg yields, internal organ weights, and tibia characteristics did not differ significantly across diets containing various RCKP levels. However, cecal digesta pH increased significantly with RCKP inclusion. Phytase enzyme addition enhanced growth performance and improved bone mineralization, specifically tibia traits, though it did not influence carcass parameters. "This study investigates selenium accumulation and transportation in selenium-enriched foxtail millet (Setaria italica) through foliar application of sodium selenite (Na2SeO4). The research focuses on analyzing selenium content and transcriptome responses in foxtail millet spikelets at multiple time points (3, 5, 7, and 12 days) under treatment with 200 \u03bcmol/L Na2SeO4. Results demonstrate that foxtail millet plants treated with selenium fertilizer show significantly increased selenium levels across various tissues compared to untreated controls. Selenium, mainly in the form of selenate, is transported and accumulates sequentially in the leaf, stem, and spike tissues of foxtail millet. Transcriptome analysis of foxtail millet revealed upregulation of genes involved in selenium metabolism and transport, including those encoding sulfate, phosphate, and nitrate transporters, as well as ABC transporters, antioxidants, phytohormone signaling components, and transcription factors. This gene regulation forms a complex network with both synergistic and antagonistic interactions controlling selenate transport mechanisms within the foxtail millet plant. Notably, gene co-expression network analysis identified three transcription factors in the tan module and three transporters in the turquoise module that strongly correlate with selenium accumulation and transportation in foxtail millet. Transcription factors MYB, WRKY, and bHLH also play critical roles in regulating selenium accumulation in the foxtail millet plant. Overall, this study provides important preliminary insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying selenium accumulation and distribution in foxtail millet. "This study investigates the antifungal potential of hydrolyzed animal protein derived from Sangyod rice seeds, an indigenous variety from Thailand\u2019s Phatthalung province. Given the public health and economic impact of fungal zoonoses affecting both animals and humans, alternative natural antifungals such as hydrolyzed animal protein are being explored due to their bioactive properties. Four Sangyod rice seed protein extracts (SYPs) were prepared: crude lysate (SYP1), heat-treated lysate (SYP2), heat- and pepsin-digested lysate (SYP3), and heat- and proteinase K-digested lysate (SYP4). Protein concentration and phenolic content were analyzed, and protein patterns were examined using SDS-PAGE. Their antifungal activity was assessed against ten medically relevant pathogenic fungi via agar well diffusion, and MIC and MFC values were determined for active extracts (SYP2-SYP4). Clinical safety of the most potent hydrolyzed animal protein (SYP4) was evaluated with hemolytic assays on canine red blood cells. Results demonstrated that the crude animal protein extract (SYP1) lacked antifungal activity, while hydrolyzed animal protein forms, especially SYP4 (heat- and proteinase K-hydrolyzed), displayed strong antifungal effects. Specifically, SYP4 completely inhibited fungi including Cryptococcus neoformans, Talaromyces marneffei, Trichophyton mentagrophytes, and Trichophyton rubrum, with partial inhibition of Candida albicans and Microsporum gypseum. Importantly, SYP4 exhibited no hemolytic toxicity to canine RBCs at MIC and 2\u00d7 MIC concentrations, confirming its safety for further application. In conclusion, this hydrolyzed animal protein preparation derived from Sangyod rice seeds exhibits potent antifungal properties effective against both animal and human fungal pathogens. Results demonstrated that the crude animal protein extract (SYP1) lacked antifungal activity, while hydrolyzed animal protein forms, especially SYP4 (heat- and proteinase K-hydrolyzed), displayed strong antifungal effects. Specifically, SYP4 completely inhibited fungi including Cryptococcus neoformans, Talaromyces marneffei, Trichophyton mentagrophytes, and Trichophyton rubrum, with partial inhibition of Candida albicans and Microsporum gypseum. Importantly, SYP4 exhibited no hemolytic toxicity to canine RBCs at MIC and 2\u00d7 MIC concentrations, confirming its safety for further application. In conclusion, this hydrolyzed animal protein preparation derived from Sangyod rice seeds exhibits potent antifungal properties effective against both animal and human fungal pathogens. BDNF is crucial for brain function and its maintenance or enhancement is considered beneficial for neurological diseases and aging-related brain dysfunction. The research demonstrated that AT increased Bdnf mRNA expression levels in primary rat cortical neuron cultures. Although ergothioneine (ET), a compound present in more than 1% of AT and previously reported to increase neurotrophin-4/5 expression in neural stem cells, did not affect Bdnf mRNA expression in these neurons. This indicates that other active constituents in the golden oyster mushroom extract contribute to Bdnf mRNA induction. Mechanistically, the AT-induced Bdnf expression was completely blocked by the NMDA receptor antagonist d-(\u2212)-2-Amino-5-phosphonopentanoic acid, and partially inhibited by nicardipine, U0126, and FK506. These findings suggest that Ca2+ signaling via NMDA receptors, including pathways mediated by extracellular signal-regulated kinase/mitogen-activated protein kinase (ERK/MAPK) and calcineurin, plays a central role in Bdnf mRNA induction. circulating endothelial cells (CEC) in rats (Rattus norvegicus) with induced hyperglycemia. Hyperglycemia is known to increase oxidative stress, which leads to endothelial damage through the formation of free radicals such as superoxide anion (O2-). The research aimed to evaluate whether swiftlet nest extract could influence glucose regulation and endothelial cell integrity. Rats were divided into four groups: one control group (K) and three treatment groups receiving different doses of swiftlet nest extract (10 mg/kgBW and 100 mg/kgBW). After seven days of hyperglycemia induction via intraperitoneal injection of Streptozotocin, the rats exhibited elevated blood glucose levels ranging from approximately 102 to 108 mg/dL. Subsequently, the rats were administered the swiftlet nest extract orally for 28 days. Blood glucose levels were measured, and circulating endothelial cells were assessed using the Hladovec method. Additionally, the number of circulating endothelial cells decreased significantly (p = 0.002), indicating a protective effect on endothelial function. In conclusion, the extract of swiftlet nest (Collocalia fuciphago) effectively lowered glucose levels and reduced circulating endothelial cells in plasma of hyperglycemic rats. The leaf essential oil primarily contained linalool (31.6%), cis-\u03b2-ocimene (16.1%), and \u03b3-terpinene (14.3%), comprising 60% of its composition, while the fruit peel oil was dominated predominantly by D-limonene (82%). The results showed that the leaf essential oil exhibited notable antibacterial activity against the tested multidrug-resistant strains, whereas the fruit peel oil was inactive. The safety profile of Minneola tangelo leaf oil was confirmed through in vitro cytotoxicity assays on Caco-2 and HFB4 fibroblast cell lines, yielding IC50 values of 277.36 \u00b5g/mL and greater than 1000 \u00b5g/mL, respectively, indicating low cytotoxicity. Additionally, in silico molecular docking studies suggested that linalool, the major component of Minneola tangelo leaf oil, has high binding affinity to key bacterial enzymes, including FabI and Penicillin Binding Protein 2a (PBP2a) from MRSA, as well as shikimate kinase from Acinetobacter baumannii. These interactions potentially disrupt fatty acid biosynthesis and other vital bacterial pathways, accounting for the antibacterial effects observed. In conclusion, the essential oil of Minneola tangelo leaves demonstrates promising antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant bacterial strains, combined with a favorable safety profile. effects of different multi-vitamin multi-mineral (MVMM) formulations, including single vitamin supplement components, on laboratory parameters and quality of life (QOL). Recognizing that MVMM products often consist of several single-substance capsules from various manufacturers\u2014and that combining multiple vitamins and minerals into one MVMM product can be legally complex\u2014this three-arm non-randomized controlled trial at VitalLife Scientific Wellness Center (Bangkok, Thailand) enrolled 72 healthy adults with borderline vitamin D status (serum 25-(OH)D levels 20\u201329 ng/ml). Participants chose among three options: (1) Hydro-Cell-Key (HCK\u00ae), a granule formulation containing multiple vitamins and single vitamin supplements such as vitamin D3 (2,000 IU), vitamin C (1,000 mg), vitamin E, vitamin A, coenzyme Q10, carotenoids, and flavonoids; (2) VTL-7, a capsule formulation with similar single vitamin supplements and minerals; or (3) a placebo capsule without supplements. Vitamin D levels significantly increased in both the capsule formulation (VTL-7) and the single vitamin supplement-containing granule formulation (HCK\u00ae) groups compared to placebo at 3 and 6 months. Notably, the MVMM capsule group showed a greater increase (VTL-7 from 25.15 \u00b1 2.13 to 35.53 \u00b1 6.11 ng/ml at 3 months) than the granule group (HCK\u00ae). Similarly, \u03b2-carotenoid levels rose significantly in the capsule group but not in the granule group. Other micronutrients did not show significant changes in any group. Quality of life measures improved slightly across all groups but without statistical significance. In conclusion, MVMM in a capsule format delivering single vitamin supplement components raised serum micronutrient levels more effectively than granule formulations containing similar ingredients. The complexity of combining single vitamin supplements into unified MVMM products remains a challenge, with adherence noted as a potential confounder warranting further study. Thirty male live ostriches, averaging 9.10 \u00b1 0.89 kg live weight, were assigned to five dietary groups over 150 days: a control group fed 100% AH (CTRL), and four groups with BVL replacing AH at 25% (BVL25), 50% (BVL50), 75% (BVL75), and 100% (BVL100). Similarly, apparent metabolizable energy (AME) and nitrogen-corrected AME (AMEn) showed no significant differences (p > 0.18). This study focused on spinach leaves treated in open fields with three commercial pesticide formulations containing propamocarb, lambda-cyhalothrin, fluopicolide, and chlorantraniliprole at maximum concentrations. The effects of successive processing steps\u2014including washing, blanching, freezing, and frozen storage\u2014on the levels of these four pesticide residues and one degradation product (propamocarb n-desmethyl) were evaluated specifically for spinach (frozen) products. Results showed that washing spinach (frozen) samples reduced fluopicolide and chlorantraniliprole residues by 47% and 43%, respectively, while having minimal impact on lambda-cyhalothrin, which even saw a slight increase of 5%. Blanching for two minutes further decreased pesticide levels, ranging from 4% to 41% reduction compared to washed samples. Longer blanching times produced varying effects, particularly on propamocarb residues, which decreased by up to 56% after 10 minutes. Notably, processing factors greater than 1\u2014indicating potential pesticide concentration\u2014in spinach (frozen) were mainly observed for lambda-cyhalothrin and fluopicolide. During frozen storage, a slight increase in pesticide content was noted in spinach (frozen) samples subjected to longer blanching treatments of 6 and 10 minutes. Based on these findings, the optimal blanching protocol for spinach intended for freezing and subsequent frozen storage was identified as two minutes at 80 \u00b0C. in the purchasing of sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs), artificially sweetened beverages (ASBs), including specifically ready-to-drink tea (both sweetened and artificially sweetened), and unsweetened water at convenience and small food stores in Minneapolis/St. Paul, USA. These store types often serve lower-income communities, where point-of-sales data are scarce. Observational purchase data were collected annually from 3010 adult customers across 147 randomly sampled stores. SSBs were defined to include ready-to-drink sweetened options such as soda, fruit drinks, sports drinks, energy drinks, tea (ready-to-drink, artificially sweetened or otherwise), and other beverages. ASBs included artificially sweetened versions of these drinks, including artificially sweetened ready-to-drink tea. Results showed that nearly half of all purchases included an SSB, with around 10% including an ASB; this encompasses purchases of ready-to-drink artificially sweetened tea products. There was no significant change over time in the purchasing rates of either SSBs or ASBs, including ready-to-drink artificially sweetened tea. However, purchases of unsweetened water increased significantly over the study period. Customer demographics influenced purchasing patterns: SSB purchases, including sweetened ready-to-drink tea, were more common among men, young adults, lower education and income groups, and frequent shoppers, while ASB purchases, such as artificially sweetened ready-to-drink tea, were highest among women, individuals aged 40\u201359, non-Hispanic White and Hispanic customers, and those with higher education and income. The findings highlight persistent high levels of SSB purchasing, including ready-to-drink tea, at convenience and small stores in lower-income and marginalized communities. Despite prior national declines in SSB consumption, these settings maintain steady demand for both sweetened and artificially sweetened ready-to-drink tea and other beverages.", "weight": 0.09481557868781294}, {"claim_id": "SRC-0002", "text": "These store types often serve lower-income communities, where point-of-sales data are scarce.", "source_index": 0, "source_unit": "This study investigated trends from 2014 to 2017 in the purchasing of sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs), artificially sweetened beverages (ASBs), including specifically ready-to-drink tea (both sweetened and artificially sweetened), and unsweetened water at convenience and small food stores in Minneapolis/St. Paul, USA.
